gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 9?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 9 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent European model consensus, including runs from the German Weather Service (DWD) and ECMWF, indicates a warm, mostly sunny day in Munich on August 9 under a high-pressure ridge with light easterly or southeasterly flow and minimal cloud cover. This setup favors strong daytime insolation and surface heating, pushing maximum temperatures into the 32–34 °C range—several degrees above the early-August climatological mean of roughly 23–25 °C. Ensemble spreads remain modest, supporting the market’s heavy weighting toward 33 °C and 34 °C outcomes, while lower probabilities on 35 °C+ reflect limited upside potential from any residual moisture or slight timing shifts in the ridge axis. Final resolution will hinge on official DWD station readings at the peak afternoon hour.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 11 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/jp/tokyo/RJTT.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Met Office forecasts indicate a sunny day across London on August 11 under building high pressure, with a projected daytime maximum of 26°C and overnight lows near 17°C. This setup favors radiative warming during clear conditions but incorporates moderating influences from a weak Atlantic flow, keeping temperatures from exceeding the mid-20s in most ensemble members. Trader consensus centers on 24–26°C outcomes because model runs show minor disagreements on cloud cover timing and boundary-layer mixing, which can shift the peak by 1–2°C. Historical August averages for the capital hover near 22–23°C, so current guidance represents above-normal but not extreme warmth, with limited risk of 28°C+ absent stronger ridging. Updated ECMWF and UKV runs expected over the next 24 hours will likely refine the exact maximum and narrow the probability distribution before market resolution.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 11 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/jp/tokyo/RJTT.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader sentiment for Tokyo's August 11 high temperature centers on short-term forecast guidance showing mostly cloudy skies with occasional scattered showers, which is expected to limit daytime heating and keep the official maximum near 28–30°C. The Japan Meteorological Agency's seasonal outlook for above-normal summer temperatures provides baseline support for values near or above the 31°C August average, yet model consensus highlights uncertainty from variable cloud cover, precipitation timing, and steering patterns that could allow brief clear periods for higher readings or enhance cooling. Historical data indicate typical midsummer highs of 30–32°C under the Pacific High, but the current setup's modest humidity and shower risk explain the market's broad distribution peaking at 29°C. Updated JMA and ensemble model runs over the next 48 hours will be the key catalysts for shifts.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent European model consensus, including runs from the German Weather Service (DWD) and ECMWF, centers on a Munich high of 33–34°C for August 10 under persistent high-pressure subsidence. This setup warms the lower atmosphere through adiabatic compression while limiting cloud cover and enabling strong daytime solar insolation. Timeanddate and other guidance align near 33°C (about 92°F), with mostly cloudy skies potentially moderating the peak. The tight 33°C–34°C split in market-implied odds reflects ensemble spread from minor variations in boundary-layer moisture, exact frontal timing, or local urban heat effects. A modest shift in any of these could tip the outcome, while probabilities for 32°C or 35°C+ remain low absent notable forecast revisions in the final 24–48 hours.
